original_question: Which voltage-gated sodium channel subunit is mutated in the autosomal dominant disorder known as paramyotonia congenita, which is characterized by paradoxical myotonia?

final_qi.question: Which voltage-gated sodium channel subunit is mutated in the autosomal dominant disorder known as paramyotonia congenita, which is characterized by paradoxical myotonia?
final_qi.long_answer: Paramyotonia congenita is an autosomal-dominant skeletal-muscle channelopathy produced by missense mutations in the SCN4A gene, which encodes the α-subunit (NaV1.4) of the skeletal muscle voltage-gated sodium channel. These mutations impair fast inactivation of the channel, leading to the hallmark paradoxical myotonia that worsens with continued activity or cold exposure.

0.question: What is the autosomal dominant disorder characterized by paradoxical myotonia?

final_answer.long_answer: Paramyotonia congenita is an autosomal-dominant muscle channelopathy caused by missense mutations in the skeletal-muscle voltage-gated sodium channel α-subunit gene SCN4A (Nav1.4). Defective inactivation of this α-subunit increases persistent Na⁺ current, producing the paradoxical myotonia that defines the disorder.
